hints: Focus on the clue that azide behaves like chloride, so start by recalling what chloride does with acidified silver nitrate.
Compare the charges of $\text{N}_3^-$ and $\text{Cl}^-$ to work out how many silver ions are needed for a neutral precipitate.
Remember what happens to fresh white $\text{AgCl}$ when dilute aqueous ammonia is added, then apply that same behaviour to the azide precipitate.
walkthrough:
**Recall the test for chloride ions**

Think of this as a familiar halide test in disguise. Chloride gives a white precipitate of silver chloride with acidified silver nitrate.

$$\text{Ag}^+(aq) + \text{Cl}^-(aq) \rightarrow \text{AgCl}(s) \text{ white precipitate}$$

**Use the analogy to find the azide precipitate formula**

Since $\text{N}_3^-$ has the same 1- charge as $\text{Cl}^-$, it needs just one $\text{Ag}^+$ to balance it. That gives a 1 to 1 formula.

$$\text{Ag}^+(aq) + \text{N}_3^-(aq) \rightarrow \text{AgN}_3(s) \text{ white precipitate}$$

**Predict the effect of aqueous ammonia**

Fresh $\text{AgCl}$ dissolves in dilute aqueous ammonia to form a colourless complex solution, $\text{[Ag(NH}_3\text{)}_2]^+$. Because azide is said to behave similarly, $\text{AgN}_3$ should do the same and dissolve to give a colourless solution.

options.A: Correct. The 1- charge of azide gives $\text{AgN}_3$, analogous to $\text{AgCl}$, and like $\text{AgCl}$ it dissolves in dilute aqueous ammonia to form the colourless diamminesilver(I) complex.
options.B: Formula is right but observation is wrong. Students choosing this may think all silver precipitates are insoluble in ammonia like $\text{AgBr}$ or $\text{AgI}$. White $\text{AgCl}$-type precipitates dissolve in dilute ammonia.
options.C: Observation is right but formula is wrong. $\text{Ag}_3\text{N}$ would imply a 3- nitride ion, $\text{N}^{3-}$. The ion here is azide, $\text{N}_3^-$, which has only a 1- charge, so only one $\text{Ag}^+$ is needed.
options.D: Both parts are wrong. This confuses azide, $\text{N}_3^-$, with nitride, $\text{N}^{3-}$, to get $\text{Ag}_3\text{N}$, and also confuses the ammonia solubility with that of $\text{AgBr}$ or $\text{AgI}$ which do not dissolve in dilute ammonia.
